thread.title_full: Isabelle Huppert Headlines Adelaide Festival 2026 as Mary, Queen of Scots

author: Sofia Alvarez
title: Isabelle Huppert Headlines Adelaide Festival 2026 as Mary, Queen of Scots
text:
I sabelle Huppert, a titan of French cinema and theater, is set to grace Australian shores in March 2026. She will bring her acclaimed one-woman show, “Mary Said What She Said,” to the Adelaide festival for an exclusive engagement.
The performance features Huppert as Mary Stuart , also known as Mary, Queen of Scots. the show, a creation of the late theatrical visionary Robert Wilson, first premiered in Paris in 2019. It delves into the life of the ill-fated Catholic monarch whose claim to the English throne put her at odds with her Protestant cousin, Queen Elizabeth I, ultimately leading to her demise.
Written by novelist Darryl Pinckney, the play is set in the period leading up to Mary Stuart’s 1587 execution for treason.It draws from her letters to construct a defense against accusations of plotting against Queen Elizabeth. Mary had spent 19 years in captivity before her execution.
Huppert is celebrated for her prolific career in film, including roles in films by directors such as Claire Denis and Michael Haneke, including the 2001 film “The Piano Teacher,” for which she received the best actress award at Cannes. Her recent work includes an appearance in the Oscar-nominated comedy “Mrs. Harris Goes to Paris.”
Robert Wilson, a distinguished theater maker and visual artist originally from Texas, gained renown for his visually striking, non-naturalistic productions. His influential works include the 1976 staging of Philip Glass’s opera “Einstein on the Beach,” a monologue adaptation of “Hamlet,” and the opera “The Black Rider: The Casting of the Magic Bullets,” a collaboration with Tom Waits and William S. Burroughs. Wilson passed away on July 31 at the age of 83.
“Mary Said What She Said” marks Huppert’s third and final stage collaboration with Wilson, whom she lauded as “a genius, one of the great, great theatre inventors of our century.”
The Adelaide festival will present “Mary Said What She Said” as a headline event,alongside performances by the French choir and orchestra Ensemble Pygmalion. The full festival program is scheduled for release on October 27.
